body:
Delivery slice PR B of 4 for #1706 (merged as squash `70d053fb7`). Migrates all nine orchestration/issue-lifecycle consumers onto the shared RIPR-SPEC-0244 selected-work/portfolio-basis contract; each consumer reuses the shared identity law engine instead of forking one. The old singleton orchestrator was retired in #1701, so these consumers are rebuilt on the new basis rather than patched in place.

## Consumer migration table

| Consumer | Issue | Spec | Command | Commit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Task/result/receipt schemas | #1633 | RIPR-SPEC-0269 | `cargo xtask work result check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` | e83b83fe5 |
| Local + durable claims | #1635 / #1647 | RIPR-SPEC-0270 | `cargo xtask work claim check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` | 982bd184b |
| Wave planning | #1634 | RIPR-SPEC-0271 | `cargo xtask work wave check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` | 760734709 |
| Role-scoped context packets | #1632 | RIPR-SPEC-0272 | `cargo xtask work context check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` | 16b3efcc4 |
| Root-thread synthesis | #1636 | RIPR-SPEC-0273 | `cargo xtask work synthesis check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` | b15168322 |
| Burn-down / closeout | #1648 | RIPR-SPEC-0274 | `cargo xtask work burndown check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` | 41cf7b0dc |
| Issue intake | #1644 | RIPR-SPEC-0275 | `cargo xtask work intake check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` | 66143feb0 |
| Plan dispositions | #1646 | RIPR-SPEC-0276 | `cargo xtask work plan check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` | fc118bac8 |
| Codex adapter delegations | #1637 / #1649 | RIPR-SPEC-0277 | `cargo xtask work adapter check [--corpus <dir>] [--json]` | 07bb01315 |

- **#1633 results**: every `WorkTaskResultV1` binds repository, portfolio-snapshot identity, basis head and the full embedded `SelectedWorkIdentityV1`; wrong repository/snapshot/issue/action/basis/worktree/head fails stale/wrong-input with the exact recompile/reconcile route; evidence-free results fail as claims; legacy refs resolve read-only with migration posture and no authority.
- **#1635/#1647 claims**: every `WorkClaimV1` binds one selected issue/action and the exact basis; claiming one item never asserts repository-wide priority (no priority/default-campaign/agent/CI-wait/progress fields exist); a stale basis keeps the claim recorded as `stale_requires_reconcile` — reconcile, never release or takeover; one worktree cannot serve two selections and one selection cannot be double-claimed; each conflict names the occupying claim and leaves it active.
- **#1634 waves**: every `WorkWavePlanV1` consumes the complete selected candidate set and partitions it into waves over the explicit resource vocabulary `campaign-record:<id>`, `portfolio-schema`, `spec-ledger`, `output-contract:<id>`, `issue:<n>`, `pr:<n>`, `worktree:<path>`; the retired generic `active-goal` resource fails closed with the explicit-vocabulary route; `portfolio-schema`/`spec-ledger` are read-only shareable references; shared exclusive resources, over-capacity waves, unassigned candidates and stale bases fail with exact routes; disjoint cross-campaign waves are admitted.
- **#1632 context packets**: every `WorkContextPacketV1` binds the selected-work identity it compiles context for; role-scoped packets stay within the recorded role/context budget; overflow is reference-first (retrieval routes, not inlined dumps); a packet for an unknown role, an unrecorded issue or a stale basis fails with exact routes.
- **#1636 synthesis**: every `WorkSynthesisV1` binds the selected transition and reports acceptance coverage rows honestly — partial coverage surfaces a named contradiction instead of a silent switch; a hidden uncovered row, a mismatched reported transition, an evidence-free synthesis or a wrong repository fails with exact routes.
- **#1648 burn-down**: every `WorkBurnDownV1` derives completion from issue/spec acceptance, implementation slices, PRs and exact-head review/proof rows; campaign and work-item records are context only and cannot override current evidence; a complete burn-down over an open or stale evidence row fails; a wrong current main, an unknown campaign record or an empty evidence set fails with exact routes.
- **#1644 intake**: every `WorkIntakeV1` binds the repository, snapshot identity, basis head, current main and one issue the captured portfolio records; campaign placement and relevant campaigns must be recorded campaigns, but an out-of-campaign issue may still qualify because placement stays a later root/planning decision; open overlapping PRs and claims stay visible before any mutation; an empty contract set, an unknown issue, a wrong repository or a legacy authority attempt fails with exact routes.
- **#1646 plan dispositions**: every `WorkPlanV1` binds the full selected-work identity it plans for and emits one closed frozen `WorkPlanDispositionV1`; planning is read-only — a row that would replace or reorder the whole portfolio fails visibly; campaign-targeting dispositions must name a recorded campaign; a blocked disposition must name its blocker; a plan derived from nothing is a claim; a wrong repository, snapshot, basis or legacy authority attempt fails with exact routes.
- **#1637/#1649 codex adapter**: every `WorkAdapterV1` delegation binds one closed project role (the six #1637 base roles plus the five #1649 issue-lifecycle roles) and one closed flow stage over the full selected-work identity; the subagent consumes the selected-work context packet plus relevant overflow and never re-reads the portfolio (`subagent_reads_portfolio` must stay `false` — portfolio compilation stays in the root thread); write-capable builder delegations require a prepared claim or isolated worktree on the bound selection; subagents never claim (`claim_write` stage fails closed); a delegation derived from nothing, or one with a wrong repository/snapshot/basis/legacy ref, fails with exact routes.

## Corpus digest fix (commit 1178aef8c)

The first gate run failed `check-fixture-contracts` with digest drift on the three earliest corpora. Root cause: the nine `work_*_identity` corpora recorded their provenance sha256 digests over Windows CRLF working-tree bytes, while `.gitattributes` pins `* text=auto eol=lf` — git stores LF blobs and CI checkouts hash LF bytes. The recorded digests were recomputed over LF bytes (now byte-equal to the git blob sha256 for all nine corpora), and the gate re-run passed end-to-end.

## Fixture coverage checklist (issue "Required fixtures")

- [x] 1 Selected issue in one campaign — result/claim corpora (9105, `campaign-rust-repair` member); reused by plan-01/plan-03 and adapter scenarios
- [x] 2 Selected issue in several related campaigns — PR A corpus reused by all corpora (9105 multi-campaign)
- [x] 3 Valid standalone work, no campaign — result-02 / claim-02 / plan-02 / adapter negatives (9106, zero campaign refs)
- [x] 4 Disjoint cross-campaign waves — wave-01 (editor-ux + rust-repair, disjoint exclusive resources); adapter-03 (1693)
- [x] 5 Open PR selected for repair — result-03 / claim-01 (9101 `repair_review`, PR 8801, `wt-9101`)
- [x] 6 Legacy packet fails to authorize a writer — PR A scenario-06 (`reject_legacy_authority`); legacy refs read-only with no authority pinned per consumer (result-04, claim-05, adapter-05 case 5)
- [x] 7 Snapshot changes, issue/head compatible — PR A scenario-07 reused; stale-basis routes pinned per consumer (result-05 case 2, claim-03 case 2, wave-05 case 0)
- [x] 8 Portfolio change introduces overlap, forces reconcile — PR A scenario-08 reused (overlap visibility law runs inside every consumer via the shared engine)
- [x] 9 Wrong repo/basis/head/... fails visibly — result-05 (8 wrong-input cases), wave-05, claim interactions, plan-05 (6 cases), adapter-05 (6 cases)
- [x] 10 Burn-down partial after merge — burndown corpus (#1648, spec 0274); PR A scenario-10 pins the projection state reused by plan-04 and adapter-05
- [x] 11 Fresh Codex root resume from artifacts — PR A scenario-11 reused; adapter-04 (reviewer resumed from committed artifacts only); no `active.toml`/chat authority bytes in any corpus (validator-pinned per consumer)
- [x] 12 Narrow one-file issue stays single-agent — wave-02 (9202 own wave despite active campaigns)

## Compatibility notes

Legacy `legacy_active_goal_ref` / `legacy_current_work_item_ref` are accepted only through explicit schema compatibility on results, claims, plans and adapter delegations: they resolve to historical/relevant campaign references, emit migration posture, and grant no write, readiness, merge or closeout authority. Corpus validators (registered in `check-fixture-contracts`) pin the read-only authority posture and fail on `active.toml`/chat references. All nine corpora reuse the committed RIPR-SPEC-0244 captured directories by relative reference — no captured bytes are duplicated — and each carries sha256-bound provenance over LF bytes.

## Verification

Per push: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy -p xtask --bins --tests -- -D warnings`, focused `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask <module>` (119 tests green across the nine modules on the final head), and `check-spec-format`, `check-spec-numbering`, `check-doc-index`, `check-traceability`, `check-fixture-contracts`, `check-command-catalog`, `check-output-contracts`, `check-changelog-fragments`, `check-static-language`, `check-file-policy`, `check-local-context`, `check-no-panic-family`, `check-allow-attributes` all pass locally. Hosted gate run (re-dispatch after the digest fix): https://github.com/EffortlessMetrics/ripr-swarm/actions/runs/39005779538 — success on head 1178aef8c.

## Non-goals / residuals for later slices

- No ripr public API change; xtask (unpublished) + fixtures + specs only.
- The actual `.codex/agents/*.toml` role definitions and `codex-prompt` compilers belong to #1637/#1649 themselves; this slice migrates only their delegation DTOs onto the selected-work basis.
- History-preserving swarm-to-`ripr` integration before release remains a separate transaction.

Refs #1706

reviews.body:
## Confirmed findings

- xtask/src/work_result_identity/tests.rs:144 — 'work_result_identity_basis_facts_for_corpus_authoring' prints AUTHORING_FACT lines but the function returns Ok(()) unconditionally. There is no assertion: the test cannot fail and the printed facts are not asserted against the committed corpus's HEAD/SNAPSHOT values. Either assert basis.repository.default_branch_sha == HEAD constant (or a pinned literal) and snapshot_identity matches the recorded SNAPSHOT_MAIN, or remove the test — it is currently smoke-only.
- `captured_worktrees` derives worktree paths from `captured.local_state`, `captured.claims`, and `captured.pull_requests`, but the corpus uses `<root>/wt-9107-a` literals while `portable_path` relativizes against `local_state.root`. If the captured root does not start with `<root>`, the relativization produces a non-portable path that silently fails the worktree-resource check. Add an assertion that `portable_path` returns a forward-slash relative path with no `<root>` placeholder, or document the exact spelling contract. (xtask/src/work_wave_identity.rs:753).
- The wave `author_corpus.py` and `work_result_identity/author_corpus.py` are not exercised in any test. If the committed JSON ever drifts from the regeneration script, the test suite passes but future regenerations silently rewrite history. Add a check that re-runs `python3 fixtures/*/author_corpus.py` in a tmp dir and diffs against committed JSON.
- 'work_claim_identity_duplicate_claim_id_fails_closed' mutates scenario.cases[1].claim.claim_id to equal case[0].claim_id, but the same test also keeps the already-present subject_identity/reconcile_selection double-claim law pinned with TWO identical violations. The test only verifies that violations.len()==2, which is true whether the duplicate-id law fires or only the double-claim law fires twice — the new duplicate-id branch is therefore not discriminated. Add a separate expect_violations tuple that pins {SubjectIdentity/RecompileBasis? no — SubjectIdentity} for duplicate-id and SubjectIdentity for double-claim, asserting the multiset exactly so a missing duplicate-id violation cannot pass. (xtask/src/work_claim_identity/tests.rs:339).
## Verification questions

- Confirm workResultCheck/WorkClaimCheck/WorkWaveCheck dispatch arms are registered but the parser pattern 'rest[2..]' silently passes extra args; --help/-h only handled inside the command not at parse time.
- Confirm mutation-negative tests rely on `crate::acquire_test_cwd_write_guard` and chdir into a sandbox, then enumerate `sandbox` for any writes outside the allowed report paths; this is sound but does not prove the underlying compiler (`compile_work_portfolio`/`load_work_captured_dir`) cannot mutate during fixture compile.
- Confirm per-spec the corpus count is 5/5/6 scenarios with 14/9/7 pinned cases; the spec-text 'Required Evidence' totals diverge (result spec claims 14, claim spec claims 9, wave spec claims 7) but the committed corpora embed those exact case counts in the JSON assertions.
- Confirm authored corpus is mostly hand-edited JSON, not regenerated by author_corpus.py.
- Confirm multiple loader-fails-closed tests rely on serde's required-field errors rather than the loader's own checks.
- Confirm sibling-path: provenance digests in committed fixture corpora pin SHA-256 of corpus.json only; SPEC.md and author_corpus.py are listed under SHA-binding convention but not separately bound here (they re-derive corpus.json). This matches the PR A pattern but is a sibling-pattern note for the proof broker rather than a defect.
## Evidence gaps

- Model proof intent was rejected by deterministic validation.
## Parked follow-ups

- test_result/test_claim/test_wave duplicate-id branch in code (WorkClaim/WorkResult/WorkWave check_* functions) is exercised only by one assertion that does not discriminate; live cargo-test receipt is pending so this is parked until green.

## Confirmed findings

- Tracing the claim_state mapping in work_claim_identity: claim_state derives from violation list length plus presence of BasisIdentity; a stale-and-conflicting claim (BasisIdentity + WorktreeIdentity) renders 'stale_requires_reconcile' because BasisIdentity wins the state string, but the Markdown prints only the first violation in its current loop, so an operator reading work-claim-check.md sees a stale_basis narrative without the worktree overlap name unless they re-read the JSON projection. Not a blocker; humans should use --json when both fire.
- RIPR-SPEC-0269 list says 'eight wrong-input failures' for result-05 but the corpus pins exactly eight cases (index 0..7), and the spec text says 'five corpus scenarios' — minor doc-vs-corpus drift worth a doc patch.
- xtask/src/command.rs:181 — XtaskCommand gains nine variants in one PR. Recommend documenting the full route list (work {result,claim,wave,context,synthesis,burndown,intake,plan,adapter} check) in PR description and README so reviewers do not under-count the delivery slice. No code change required.
- xtask/src/work_result_identity/tests.rs:99 — `work_result_identity_basis_facts_for_corpus_authoring` test only prints AUTHORING_FACT lines and returns Ok(()) without asserting the basis facts against committed corpus values. Per the seeded review summary it is smoke-only. Recommend adding a pinned assertion (default_branch_sha matches recorded HEAD constant and snapshot_identity matches recorded SNAPSHOT_MAIN) or removing the test.
- xtask/src/work_wave_identity.rs:110 — captured_worktrees() derives worktree spellings from local_state.root via portable_path, but corpus fixtures use literal '<root>/wt-9107-a' paths — if local_state.root does not start with the literal '<root>' placeholder the relativized path silently fails the worktree-resource check.
## Verification questions

- Confirm work_claim_identity reuses crate::work_selection_identity::issue_identity referenced via fully-qualified path in legacy_current_work_item_ref check; sourcing is consistent with sibling modules.
- Confirm xtask/src/work_burndown_identity.rs:1023 — Validate path: digest-drift failure branch in validate_work_burndown_identity_fixture_corpus emits 'work-result:sha256:{}' in its formatted message — copy-pasted from work_result_identity. While the provenance is consumed only for human-readable diagnostics, the literal prefix 'work-result' next to a burn-down fixture drift would mislead the next operator reading check-fixture-contracts output. Should report `work-burndown:sha256:` so the prefix matches the corpus identity.
- Confirm xtask uses acquire_test_cwd_write_guard for sandbox CWD tests but the guard definition and BlindJourney::sha256_hex live in modules outside this diff; cannot verify ordering guarantees.
- Confirm seeded review thread raised the PR-scope mismatch (three vs seven consumers) and a missing smoke-only claim_facts_for_corpus_authoring test on work_result_identity. Both are resolved at lane scope: the scope question is policy/docs not test oracle; the AUTHORING_FACT test prints but never asserts.
## Refuted

- Sibling evidence paths prove this slice safe despite the ripr sensor failing.; refuted because: Available structural witnesses (tokmd, unsafe-review, ast-grep) do not by themselves cover the nine-corpus behavioral surface; safety remains a parked follow-up until cargo-test (scheduled-late) and a green ripr receipt land. Reporting it as covered would be a false-premise approval.
## Evidence gaps

- ripr sensor failed (exit code 2); planned but did not produce a receipt. Three sibling evidence paths (gitleaks/osv-scanner/cargo-audit) also skipped by config, leaving only unsafe-review, ast-grep and tokmd receipts as available structural witnesses for this diff.
## Parked follow-ups

- No divergent sibling helper tree detected. Each consumer mirrors the RIPR-SPEC-0244 pattern: schema DTO + CorpusV1 + load_*_corpus + CheckViewV1 + check_*_engine + run_*_check + write_report + validate_*_fixture_corpus. Helper duplication risk is parked, not blocker.

title: feat(orch): migrate orchestration consumers to selected-work portfolio basis (#1706 PR B)
